text:
A: Hiya, you alright? Haider.
B: Alright, mate. Darren. You're the one with the Chelsea scarf, aren't you?
A: That's me. Guilty. What about you, who d'you support?
B: Bristol City. Don't laugh.
A: I'm not laughing, mate. At least you're not managed by a revolving door. We've had about four managers since I last looked.
B: Ha. True enough. I don't get to Ashton Gate no more, mind. Too dear. Watch it down the pub mostly, or on me phone.
A: Same, I watch it at my cousin's flat. Cheaper and he's got the big telly. Where are you, then?
B: Bridgwater. Somerset. You?
A: Hanwell, west London. Ealing way.
B: Never been. I've been up London about three times in my life, I reckon. What d'you do?
A: IT, at a college. I look after the Wi-Fi, the network, the projectors, all that. Calm job mostly, until enrolment day when the Wi-Fi goes down and two hundred teenagers look at you like you've ruined their life.
B: Ha! I bet. I'm a cleaner, part-time, at a supermarket. Early shifts. Floors, bins, staff toilets, the glamorous stuff.
A: Early like how early?
B: Up at half four.
A: Half four? Nah. Respect, mate. I can't do that.
B: You get used to it. Sort of. I'm knackered by dinner time, mind, but nobody hovers over you at that hour, that's the good bit. I used to do warehouse work, forklifts and that, but me back went, and me knee, so.
A: Your back as well? Mine went two years ago. Disc. I used to play five-a-side every Wednesday, ten years, then that was it. Now I just walk the canal.
B: Ah, mate, that's young for that. I'm fifty, I'm allowed. I was just talking to the bloke before, Tomasz, he's got a bad back an' all. We're all falling apart, this lot.
A: Ha, it's a support group. Sit in the car too long and that's it for me, I'm walking like a penguin.
B: Tell me about it. What car you got?
A: 2014 Corolla. Needs its MOT soon, I'm praying, honestly.
B: Corollas, they'll go forever, them. You'll be fine. I've got a moped in me shed I've been doing up. Six years.
A: Six years? What's left on it?
B: Er, depends who you ask. Karen'd say all of it. I'd say the carb and a bit of wiring. Then it's done. Proper job.
A: Wiring I can help you with, to be fair. Well, sort of. Computers, not mopeds.
B: Ha, close enough, mate. You got a family, kids?
A: No kids. I live with my mum and my brother. My mum and my aunties keep asking when I'm getting married, so I've got a whole list of jokes ready for that.
B: Ha! Give 'em one, then.
A: Usually I just say, the Corolla's my wife, and my mum hits me with a slipper.
B: Ha, that's good, that is. My lot are grown up now, both moved out. I've got a granddaughter in Bristol, she's two. Best thing that's happened, honestly. Changes you, d'you know what I mean? Makes you think about stuff.
A: Yeah, I get that. My sister's kids are round every Sunday, they wreck my PlayStation controllers, but, you know, you can't be angry. What's her name, your—
